prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Reform UK Manifesto 2024 – Summary (under 500 words)

Overview
- Reform UK argues the Conservative and Labour parties have failed, citing high taxes, debt, immigration, crime, NHS waits and Net Zero costs. It proposes a “Contract with You” focused on sovereignty, border control, tax cuts, public service reform and domestic energy production.

Core pledges
- Freeze non-essential immigration and stop small boats.
- End NHS waiting lists while keeping care free at point of use.
- Make work pay: raise the income tax threshold to £20,000.
- Cut energy bills: scrap Net Zero and green levies; expand oil and gas.
- Restore law and order and protect British culture, identity and values.

Key policies by area
- Immigration: Freeze non-essential visas; leave the ECHR; detain/deport illegal arrivals and return small boats to France; bar student dependents; 5-year residency to access benefits; employer immigration tax (+6.2 pp NI to 20% for foreign workers, with exemptions). Claimed savings: £5–10bn pa; employer tax £4bn pa.
- Government waste: Stop paying interest on QE reserves (£35bn pa); 5% efficiency saving across departments (£50bn pa); cut foreign aid by 50% (£6bn); deregulation and better tax collection. Total “potential savings” claimed: £91bn pa.
- Economy (personal): Lift income tax start point to £20k; higher rate at £70k; cut fuel duty by 20p; scrap VAT on energy and green levies; large Stamp Duty cuts; restore VAT-free tourist shopping; abolish IHT below £2m, 20% above. Cost: £70bn pa.
- Economy (business): Raise CT threshold to £100k; cut CT to 20% then 15% by year 3; abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k; later abolish business rates for high-street SMEs, offset by 4% online delivery tax; planning and red-tape reform. Cost: £18bn pa.
- NHS: Zero waiting lists via staff tax breaks (zero basic rate for 3 years), end training caps, loan write-offs for service; use independent capacity; 20% tax relief on private healthcare; vouchers if NHS wait targets missed; efficiency drive; inquiry on excess deaths/vaccine harms. Cost: £17bn pa.
- Net Zero/energy: Scrap Net Zero and renewables subsidies; fast-track North Sea oil/gas and shale trials; expand nuclear SMRs. Claimed savings: £30bn pa.
- Policing/justice: Recruit 40,000 officers; zero-tolerance policing; end DE&I roles; mandatory life for violent repeat offenders; 10,000 new prison places; more courts and staff. Costs: policing £3bn pa; justice £2bn pa.
- Education: “Patriotic curriculum”; ban transgender ideology in schools; 20% tax relief on independent education; scrap student loan interest; enforce free speech and expand PRUs. Cost: £5bn pa.
- Benefits: Tougher work requirements (2-strike rule), face-to-face assessments, incentives for apprenticeships. Claimed savings: £15bn pa.
- Brexit: Scrap retained EU law; abandon Windsor Framework; prepare to renegotiate EU TCA; keep UK forces independent of EU structures.
- Defence: Raise spend to 2.5% of GDP by year 3 and 3% within 6 years; pay rise; Armed Forces Justice Bill; dedicated veterans department. Cost: £14bn pa.
- Housing: Fast-track brownfield; prioritize locals for social housing; scrap Section 24 for landlords; drop Renters’ Reform Bill. Neutral cost.
- Families: Transferable marriage allowance (target 25%); front-load child benefit for ages 1–4; mandate single-sex spaces; tighter smartphone controls for children. Cost: £8bn pa.
- Transport/infrastructure: Scrap HS2 (save £25bn one-off); end ULEZ/LTNs and most 20mph zones; new utilities ownership model (50% public/50% UK pensions). Savings: £5bn pa (plus £25bn one-off).
- Agriculture/fisheries: Increase farm budget to £3bn; scrap climate-linked farm subsidies; restrict foreign fishing; build UK processing; revive fleets. Costs: agriculture £2bn pa; fisheries £2bn pa.
- Pensions/social care: Royal Commission on social care; curb offshore tax avoidance in care; fix Mineworkers’ Pension.
- Constitutional/culture: Leave ECHR; reform Lords/civil service/postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights; scrap Equalities Act DE&I rules; Free Speech Bill; scrap BBC licence fee; oppose WHO treaty and CBDC; anti-corruption unit.

Funding (claims)
- Savings and extra growth: £160bn pa (incl. £150bn savings + £10bn tax from higher growth).
- Total costs: £141bn pa. Reform UK says this funds its programme.
